practice_description.medium: writing, curatorial practice, performance, digital culture criticism
practice_description.practice_summary: Writer, curator, and theorist whose work explores the intersection of digital identity, gender, race, and technology, arguing that the glitch — the failure, the error, the refusal to be categorized — is a site of radical liberation and creative possibility.
practice_description.methodology: Russell works across curatorial practice, critical writing, and public programming. Her methodology centers on centering marginalized voices in digital culture discourse, using the glitch as both metaphor and method. She draws on Black feminist theory, queer theory, and digital culture studies to build a framework for resistance through technological failure and refusal. As Executive Director and Chief Curator of The Kitchen in New York, she embeds theory in institutional practice.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Russell's concept of the glitch as productive failure and resistance to categorization is directly relevant to A(DAI)'s need to handle frontier signals — work that refuses neat classification and challenges the graph's taxonomic impulses.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Her theoretical work does not produce visual substrate directly, but her curatorial practice foregrounds artworks that function as glitches within systems — these works could serve as substrate that disrupts and reconfigures generative compositions.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Her framework is inherently relational — the glitch exists in relation to the system it disrupts. This maps onto graph-based thinking where edges (relations) are as important as nodes, and where breakdowns in connection are themselves meaningful.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: The glitch is by definition a moment of recomposition — when a system breaks, it reconfigures. Russell's framework suggests that a generative exhibition should embrace rather than suppress these moments of failure and reconfiguration.

works.title: Glitch Feminism: A Manifesto
works.description: Book arguing that the glitch — digital error, system failure — is a site of liberation for bodies that don't conform to binary categories. Proposes the glitch as a methodology for resisting surveillance, categorization, and control.
works.relevance: Foundational text for understanding how frontier signals that resist classification should be handled in A(DAI)'s intelligence infrastructure — not as errors to be corrected but as productive disruptions.

works.title: Glitch Feminism (expanded edition / ongoing curatorial program)
works.description: Continued development of glitch feminism through curatorial programming at The Kitchen, public lectures, and collaborative projects extending the manifesto into institutional practice.
works.relevance: Demonstrates how theoretical frameworks can be embedded in institutional governance and curatorial decision-making — a model for A(DAI)'s own integration of theory into practice.

works.title: The Kitchen curatorial program
works.description: As Executive Director and Chief Curator of The Kitchen, Russell has programmed interdisciplinary work spanning performance, video, sound, and digital art that embodies glitch feminism principles.
works.relevance: Institutional model for how a commons-oriented art space can center resistance, glitch, and refusal within its programming framework.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Russell's institutional leadership at The Kitchen represents a form of protocol design — she is reshaping how an art institution operates, what it values, and who it centers. The governance of the institution becomes a creative act.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: The Kitchen's curatorial and programming framework under Russell's direction functions as a designed system for centering marginalized voices in contemporary art.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Russell's work is oriented toward openness and accessibility in discourse, though published through traditional channels (Verso Books). Her curatorial practice at The Kitchen emphasizes public access and community engagement. The glitch feminism framework itself is a commons-oriented intellectual tool designed to be taken up and extended by others.

governance_model.governance_detail: As Executive Director and Chief Curator of The Kitchen, Russell operates within an institutional governance structure while exercising significant curatorial autonomy. Her solo writing practice is individually governed.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Her curatorial practice involves collaborative consent with artists and performers. Her writing engages with and credits digital culture practitioners and theorists whose work she discusses.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Solo authorship for written works, collaborative and collective for curatorial projects. Credits and centers the artists and communities she works with.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Written works are fixed upon publication. Curatorial programs are durational and evolve over institutional seasons. The theoretical framework is designed to be living and applicable to emerging conditions.

data_materiality.data_sources: Digital culture, social media, online communities, Black feminist theory, queer theory, contemporary art practice
data_materiality.data_provenance: Published sources, public digital culture, community-generated discourse

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Russell's work does not directly engage with technical embedding spaces, but her concept of the glitch is highly relevant to understanding what happens at the boundaries and failure points of embedding spaces — where categorization breaks down and novel meaning emerges.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Yes — her curatorial work spans performance, video, sound, text, and digital media.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Through The Kitchen, Russell programs work that spans gallery installation, performance, screening, and digital presentation. Her theoretical work circulates through publishing, lectures, and public discourse.

interoperability.composability: The glitch feminism framework is highly composable — it can be applied as a lens, a design principle, or a curatorial methodology across different systems and contexts.
interoperability.technical_openness: Open conceptual framework, published through traditional academic/trade channels.

technical_approach.stack: No specific technical stack. Engages critically with digital platforms, social media, and surveillance technologies as objects of analysis and sites of resistance.

network_position.scene_affiliation: New York contemporary art, digital culture theory, Black feminist technology studies, performance art, The Kitchen community, Verso Books intellectual network
network_position.connections: Kate Crawford (critical technology studies), McKenzie Wark (digital culture theory), James Bridle (technology criticism)

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Russell's glitch feminism provides a critical framework for how A(DAI) handles signals that resist classification. Her work should inform the system's approach to frontier signals and the design of taxonomies that can accommodate refusal and ambiguity. Could also serve as a conversation partner on questions of identity, categorization, and resistance in collective intelligence systems.
